topic: How colour vision works: The biology of cone cells explained
title: How Colour Vision Works: The Biology Explained
false_sentence: Step three: each cone cell absorbs a different wavelength from the red apple, sending nerve signals to your brain.
correct_version: A red apple reflects mostly long wavelengths; these stimulate your long-wavelength (red) cones significantly, while medium and short-wavelength cones are stimulated less. It is the specific pattern of relative activation across all three cone types that your brain interprets as the color red.
why: The narration implies each cone type only absorbs 'a' wavelength (singular) and that red cones are the only ones responding to a red apple, which is inaccurate; color perception relies on the ratio of activation across all three cone types.
